extracted.intended_audience: Competent Authorities of Contracting Parties, applicants/beneficiaries seeking international registration of appellations of origin or geographical indications, and International Bureau/WIPO staff and legal practitioners handling such registrations
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing filing, examination, fees, registration, refusal, amendments, finances and accession under the Geneva Act of the Lisbon Agreement and its Regulations, as applicable to international registrations of appellations of origin and geographical indications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation of Director General and staff in Assembly and bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Any staff member designated by the Director General shall participate, without the right to vote, in all meetings of the Assembly, the committees and working groups established by the Assembly. The Director General, or a staff member designated by him, shall be ex officio Secretary of such a body. The Director General and persons designated by him shall take part, without the right to vote, in the discussions at revision conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau preparations for revision conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall, in accordance with the directions of the Assembly, make the preparations for any revision conferences and may consult with intergovernmental and international and national non-governmental organizations concerning the said preparations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget transparency for the Special Union
rubrics_metrics.description: The income and expenses of the Special Union shall be reflected in the budget of the Organization in a fair and transparent manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of financing of the Special Union
rubrics_metrics.description: The income of the Special Union shall be derived from: (i) fees collected under Article 7(1) and (2); (ii) proceeds from sale of, or royalties on, International Bureau publications; (iii) gifts, bequests, and subventions; (iv) rent, investment revenue, and other income; (v) special contributions of Contracting Parties or alternative sources if receipts from (i)-(iv) do not suffice, as decided by the Assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixing of fees and budget level
rubrics_metrics.description: Amounts of the fees shall be fixed by the Assembly on the proposal of the Director General and shall be so fixed that, together with other income, revenue should be sufficient to cover the expenses of the International Bureau for maintaining the international registration service. If the Program and Budget is not adopted before a new financial period, authorization to incur obligations/payments remains at previous financial period level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of contribution classes and weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting Party shall belong to the same contribution class as in the Paris Convention (or as it would belong if it were a Party). Intergovernmental organizations are class I unless otherwise decided. Contributions shall be partially weighted according to number of registrations originating in the Contracting Party, as decided by the Assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working capital fund for the Special Union
rubrics_metrics.description: The Special Union shall have a working capital fund constituted by advance payments by each member when decided; Assembly may increase it; proportions and terms fixed by the Assembly on the Director General's proposal. Surplus income may permit repayment proportionate to initial payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advances by host State under headquarters agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Headquarters agreement shall provide that, whenever the working capital fund is insufficient, the host State shall grant advances; amounts and conditions are subject to separate agreements. Either the State or the Organization may denounce the obligation to grant advances with three years' effect after notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditing of accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditing shall be effected by one or more States members of the Special Union or by external auditors, as provided in the Financial Regulations. They shall be designated, with their agreement, by the Assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations establish details for carrying out the Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The details for carrying out the Act shall be established in the Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment thresholds for provisions of the Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly may decide that certain provisions of the Regulations may be amended only by unanimity or only by a three-fourths majority. To remove or apply such special majority requirements in the future, the Assembly must act by unanimity (to remove) or by a three‑fourths majority (to apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict between Act and Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of conflict between the provisions of the Act and those of the Regulations, the Act shall prevail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision of the Act by Diplomatic Conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: This Act may be revised by Diplomatic Conferences of the Contracting Parties. The convocation of any Diplomatic Conference shall be decided by the Assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment procedure for Articles 22–24 and 27 by the Assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for amendment of Articles 22–24 and Article 27 may be initiated by any Contracting Party or the Director General and must be communicated at least six months in advance. Adoption requires a three‑fourths majority, except amendments to Article 22 and the present paragraph require a four‑fifths majority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry into force rules: generally one month after written notifications of acceptance by three‑fourths of Contracting Parties who were members of the Assembly at adoption; special non‑acceptance rules apply to certain subparagraphs and may prevent entry into force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becoming party — eligibility and modes (ratification/accession)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility: (i) any State party to the Paris Convention may sign and become party; (ii) other States members of the Organization may become party if they declare legislation complies with Paris Convention provisions concerning appellations of origin/geographical indications/trademarks; (iii) intergovernmental organizations may become party provided at least one member State is party to the Paris Convention and the organization is duly authorized and its constituting treaty allows regional protection titles. Parties may deposit an instrument of ratification (if signed) or accession (if not signed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective date rules apply (Article 28(3)); special rules for intergovernmental organizations whose domestic protection is based on internal treaties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of ratifications/accessions and entry into force
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective date of deposit is generally the date the instrument is deposited, with special rules for certain intergovernmental organizations (see Article 28(3)). This Act enters into force three months after five eligible parties have deposited instruments. Parties depositing ≥3 months before entry into force become bound on entry into force; others become bound three months after deposit or later date indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International registrations effected prior to accession may be subject to the Act in that territory, subject to Article 7(4) and Chapter IV; acceding parties may specify extensions of certain time limits via declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: No reservations to this Act are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relations with Lisbon Agreement and 1967 Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Where States are party to both this Act and the Lisbon Agreement or the 1967 Act, this Act alone applies as regards mutual relations of such States, but States must accord no lower protection than required by the Lisbon Agreement/1967 Act with respect to registrations effective under those instruments. States party to both shall continue to apply Lisbon/1967 Act in relations with States that are not party to this Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denunciation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Contracting Party may denounce the Act by notification to the Director General. Denunciation takes effect one year after receipt or on a later date indicated; it does not affect pending applications or international registrations in force at coming into effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages and signature of the Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act shall be signed in a single original in English, Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian and Spanish, all texts equally authentic. Official texts in other languages may be established by the Director General after consultation. The Act remains open for signature at the Organization's headquarters for one year after adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositary
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director General shall be the depositary of this Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1 — definitions and abbreviated expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviated expressions defined in Article 1 have the same meaning in the Regulations; 'Rule' refers to a rule of these Regulations; 'Administrative Instructions' means the Administrative Instructions referred to in Rule 24; 'Official Form' means a form drawn up by the International Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 2 — calculation of time limits (years/months/non-working days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Periods in years expire in the subsequent year on the same day and month (Feb 29 → Feb 28). Periods in months expire on same day number in subsequent month, or last day if that day number does not exist. If a period expires on a day that is not a working day for the International Bureau or Competent Authority, it expires on the first subsequent working day for that entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 3 — working languages for applications and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Application shall be in English, French or Spanish. Subsequent communications concerning an application or international registration shall be in English, French or Spanish at the choice of the Competent Authority concerned (or, for Article 5(3), at the choice of beneficiaries or the natural person/legal entity). Any translation needed for procedures shall be made by the International Bureau. Entries in the International Register and publication shall be in English, French and Spanish, translated by the International Bureau, except the International Bureau shall not translate the appellation of origin or geographical indication. Where the application contains a transliteration of the appellation/geographical indication per Rule 5(2)(b), the International Bureau shall not check whether the transliteration is correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 4 — notification and role of the Competent Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon accession, each Contracting Party shall notify the International Bureau of the name/contact details of its Competent Authority (the authority designated to present applications and receive notifications). The Competent Authority shall make available information on procedures for enforcement of rights. Preferably a single Competent Authority; if multiple, notification must indicate respective competences. Contracting Parties must notify modifications; International Bureau may take cognizance ex officio where clear indications of change exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5(1) — filing formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall be filed with the International Bureau on the Official Form and shall be signed by the Competent Authority presenting it or, in the case of Article 5(3), by the beneficiaries or the natural person or legal entity referred to in Article 5(2)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5(2) — mandatory contents of the application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall indicate: (i) the Contracting Party of Origin; (ii) the Competent Authority presenting the application or details identifying the beneficiaries or the natural person/legal entity (Article 5(3) case); (iii) the beneficiaries (collective or by name) or the natural person/legal entity with legal standing under law of Contracting Party of Origin; (iv) the appellation of origin or geographical indication for which registration is sought, in the official language(s) of the Contracting Party of Origin as contained in the registration/act/decision granting protection in that Party; (v) the good(s) to which the appellation/geographical indication applies, as precisely as possible; (vi) the geographical area of origin or production; (vii) identifying details including date of registration or legislative/administrative/judicial decision granting protection in the Contracting Party of Origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 5(2)(iv) and (b) subject to Rule 3(3) and (4) (translations/transliterations exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5(2)(b) — transliteration requirement for non-Latin characters
rubrics_metrics.description: If names/geographical area/appellation are not in Latin characters, the application shall include a transliteration using the phonetics of the language of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The International Bureau will not check whether the transliteration is correct (Rule 3(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5(2)(c) — payment of registration and other fees with application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall be accompanied by the registration fee and any other fees, as specified in Rule 8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5(3) — particulars on quality, reputation or characteristics when required
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Contracting Party requires that the application indicate particulars concerning, for appellation of origin: the quality/characteristics of the good and its connection with the geographical environment; and for geographical indication: the quality/reputation/other characteristic and its connection with the geographical area, it shall notify the Director General. Such particulars shall be provided in a working language but will not be translated by the International Bureau. An application not in accordance with such notified requirement shall, subject to Rule 6, have the effect that protection is renounced in respect of that Contracting Party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5(4) — signature and/or declaration of intention to use when required
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Contracting Party requires signature by a person having legal standing to assert rights or requires a declaration of intention to use or to exercise control over use, it shall notify the Director General. An application not signed or not accompanied by required declaration shall, subject to Rule 6, have the effect that protection is renounced in respect of that Contracting Party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5(5) — indication of elements for which protection is not claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall indicate whether, to the best knowledge of the applicant, the registration/act/decision granting protection in the Contracting Party of Origin specifies that protection is not granted for certain elements of the appellation or geographical indication; any such elements shall be indicated in a working language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5(6) — optional contents of the application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application may indicate or contain: (i) addresses of beneficiaries; (ii) a declaration that protection is renounced in one or more Contracting Parties; (iii) a copy in original language of the registration/act/decision granting protection in the Contracting Party of Origin; (iv) a statement that protection is not claimed for certain other elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 6(1) — examination and correction of irregular applications, three‑month remedy period
rubrics_metrics.description: If the International Bureau finds that an application does not satisfy conditions of Rule 3(1) or Rule 5, it shall defer registration and invite the Competent Authority or beneficiaries to remedy the irregularity within three months from the invitation date. If irregularity not corrected within two months, IB sends a reminder (no effect on three‑month period). If not corrected within three months, the application shall (subject to (d)) be rejected by IB, which shall inform the Competent Authority/beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If irregularity concerns a requirement based on a notification under Rule 5(3) or (4) or Article 7(4), and not corrected, protection will be considered renounced in that Contracting Party. Where application is rejected, IB shall refund fees after deduction of an amount equal to half the registration fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 6(2) — application not considered if not filed by Competent Authority or authorized person
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is not filed by the Competent Authority of the Contracting Party of Origin or, in the case of Article 5(3), by the beneficiaries or the natural person/legal entity referred to in Article 5(2)(ii), it shall not be considered as such by the International Bureau and shall be returned to the sender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 7(1) — conditions for entry in the International Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the International Bureau finds the application satisfies Rules 3(1) and 5, it shall enter the appellation or geographical indication in the International Register. Where governed also by the Lisbon Agreement or 1967 Act, IB shall enter if it satisfies the corresponding rules. IB shall indicate per Contracting Party whether the registration is governed by this Act or by the Lisbon Agreement/1967 Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 7(2) — required contents of the international registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The international registration shall contain or indicate: (i) all particulars given in the application; (ii) the language in which IB received the application; (iii) the number of the international registration; (iv) the date of the international registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 7(3) — certificate of international registration and notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall send a certificate of international registration to the Competent Authority of the Contracting Party of Origin or to the beneficiaries or natural person/legal entity who requested registration, and notify the international registration to the Competent Authority of each Contracting Party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 7(4) — treatment of registrations from Lisbon Agreement/1967 Act on accession
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon ratification/accession by a State party to the Lisbon Agreement/1967 Act, Rule 5(2)–(4) shall apply mutatis mutandis to international registrations/effective appellations; IB shall verify with Competent Authority any modifications needed for registration under this Act and notify international registrations to all other Contracting Parties. Modifications subject to fee. Declarations of refusal/notification of invalidation issued under Lisbon/1967 Act remain effective under this Act unless withdrawn; other Contracting Parties shall continue to protect the appellation under this Act unless they indicate otherwise. Periods granted under Lisbon/1967 Act remain subject to Article 17 for their remainder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 8(1) — fees to be collected by the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall collect fees payable in Swiss francs including: (i) fee for international registration; (ii) fee for each modification; (iii) fee for providing an extract from the International Register; (iv) fee for providing an attestation or other written information concerning Register contents; (v) individual fees as referred to in paragraph (2). (Actual amounts to be decided by the Assembly.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 8(2) — establishment and conversion of individual fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a Contracting Party makes a declaration wanting to receive an individual fee in its currency, amount shall be indicated in that currency. If indicated in a currency other than Swiss francs, the Director General shall establish the amount in Swiss francs on the basis of the UN official exchange rate. If exchange rate fluctuates ±5% for more than three months, Competent Authority may request new Swiss franc amount to be established; Director General shall proceed and fix applicability date between one and two months after publication. If rate lower by ≥10% for more than three months, Director General shall establish new Swiss franc amount (applicability date likewise between one and two months after publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 8(3) — crediting of individual fees to Contracting Parties' accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual fee paid to the International Bureau in respect of a Contracting Party shall be credited to that Contracting Party's account with the International Bureau within the month following the month in which recording of the international registration for which the fee was paid was effected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 8(4) — obligation to use Swiss currency for payments to IB
rubrics_metrics.description: All payments made under these Regulations to the International Bureau shall be in Swiss currency irrespective of the fact that Competent Authorities may have collected those fees in another currency when forwarding them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 8(5) — payment through Competent Authority permitted if accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to exceptions, fees shall be paid directly to the International Bureau. Fees payable in connection with an application may be paid through the Competent Authority if that Authority accepts to collect and forward such fees and the beneficiaries so wish; any Competent Authority which accepts must notify the Director General.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 8(6) — modes of payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees shall be paid to the International Bureau in accordance with the Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 8(7) — indications accompanying the payment
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of payment of any fee to the International Bureau an indication must be given of the appellation of origin or geographical indication concerned and the purpose of the payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 8(8) — date of payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any fee shall be considered to have been paid to the International Bureau on the day on which the International Bureau receives the required amount. If the amount is available in an account opened with IB and IB has received instructions to debit it, the fee is considered paid on the day IB receives an application or request for recording a modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 8(9) — change in the amount of the fees applies by receipt date
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amount of any fee is changed, the amount valid on the date on which the fee was received by the International Bureau shall be applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 9(1) — form and time limit for refusal notification
rubrics_metrics.description: A refusal shall be notified to the International Bureau by the Competent Authority of the concerned Contracting Party and shall be signed by that Competent Authority. The refusal shall be notified within a period of one year from the receipt of the notification of international registration under Article 6(4). In the case of Article 29(4), this time limit may be extended by another year.
